data.title: ADR-008: Where the landing page lives
body: # ADR-008: Where the landing page lives
- **Status:** accepted
- **Scope:** repository, marketing, deployment
## Context

It has been settled that we are making a landing page: Next.js + Tailwind + Motion, hosting on Vercel, our own domain. The question arises of where its code lies — in this repository or in a separate one.

[ADR-007](DOC-10) already gave the rule and one question for every new file: **will somebody else be able to reproduce or understand the product without it?** The landing page does not pass that check — the CLI is fully understandable and reproducible without a single line of the site.

Scale matters too. Next.js with Tailwind and Motion means its own `package.json`, its own lock file, its own CI, build configs and, most importantly, **binary assets**: demo video, posters, og images. In a repository that was just cut from 491 files to 94 precisely so that a clone would not drag somebody else's things along, an mp4 of a few megabytes is exactly the same mistake in a new wrapper.
## Alternatives considered
| Option | Pros | Cons |

| A `site/` folder in this repository | The numbers and the copy are versioned together with the product; one PR changes both | Violates ADR-007; video in the product's git; the product's diff drowns in marketing; on Vercel a Root Directory and an Ignored Build Step are needed |

| **A separate repository `kadence-site`** | Repository = the product, as already decided; a separate Vercel project with no workaround settings; the product's issues and stars do not get mixed with marketing ones | The numbers on the page can diverge from the tests |
| A `gh-pages` branch | Zero new repositories | The worst of both: the site's history inside the product's history, and inconvenient to work with |
## Decision
**A separate repository `kadence-site`.** The product repository stays the product.

The argument that "the numbers are taken from the same tests" turned out to be weaker than it seemed: in a shared repository they would be copied by hand anyway. So we take that price off with an explicit mechanism, not with the files being neighbours:
1. In the site, all the numbers lie in one file `content/facts.json` — each with a `source` field (a path to the test or the document that holds it).
2. A line is added to the product's release checklist: **update `facts.json` if the size, the startup time or the probe data have changed**.

3. When this starts being forgotten — a GitHub Action in the product publishes the benchmark as a release artefact, and the site reads it at build time. It is not worth doing in advance: while there are few releases, this is complexity without a need.
## Consequences

- Positive: `git clone` of the product still gives only the product; the site freely pulls in any dependencies and assets without asking ADR-007's permission; deployment on Vercel is standard, without a Root Directory and an Ignored Build Step.
- Cost: two repositories instead of one, and the numbers have to be synchronised deliberately.

- What will have to be reconsidered: if the site grows into documentation generated from the code (`--help`, the JSON schema) — then the generator has to live in the product, and the site consumes its output as a package or an artefact. That is no reason to move the site back.
## While the repository does not exist

The code is prepared in a `site/` directory on disk, which **does not get into git** of this repository — the same way as `.claude/`. When the directory is ready, a separate repository is made from it. The line in `.gitignore` exists exactly for this period and is removed together with the directory.
